pullRequest.title: feat(linear): show, edit and launch assigned Linear tickets
pullRequest.body:
## Résumé

Étape 3 de la spec Canopy : le connecteur Linear. Les tickets Linear qui me sont assignés apparaissent dans l'écran Tickets, mélangés aux tickets locaux. On peut les modifier (commentaires compris) et les lancer comme un ticket local. Tout passe par le serveur MCP officiel de Linear, parce que l'espace pro bloque les clés API.

- **Connexion** : Réglages → « Connecter Linear ». OAuth du serveur MCP avec enregistrement dynamique du client, PKCE et `state` vérifié. Le serveur de retour écoute uniquement sur la boucle locale. Le jeton est chiffré avec `safeStorage`. Une connexion expirée ou hors ligne est reconnue comme telle, jamais comme une déconnexion.
- **Liste** : une seule liste groupée par statut, avec un badge Linear ou Local, et des filtres statut, source, priorité et recherche. L'en-tête indique « Linear · synchro il y a N min » avec ⟳. Le cache est gardé sur disque : une erreur ne vide jamais la liste. Un ticket qui part de la liste est signalé une fois avec sa raison (réassigné, annulé, introuvable). Les tickets lancés et ceux qui ont des modifications en attente restent affichés.
- **Éditeur** : titre, description, statut (les vrais statuts de l'équipe), priorité, étiquettes, assigné, sous-tickets, commentaires, « Ouvrir dans Linear ».
  - La description part à la sortie du champ, en modifications partielles (`save_issue` + `patch`). La modification d'un collègue ailleurs dans le texte est préservée ; sur le même passage, les deux versions sont affichées et on choisit.
  - Les étiquettes sont envoyées en différences, pour ne pas retirer celle d'un collègue.
- **File d'attente** : toute modification est écrite sur disque avant l'envoi et renvoyée quand Linear redevient joignable. Elle n'est jamais appliquée deux fois après une réponse perdue. Seul le champ bloqué est retenu, les autres partent.
- **Lancement** : branche `feat/<id>-<titre>`. Le prompt contient l'identifiant, l'URL et la description, et indique que le reste est accessible via le MCP Linear. Rien n'est écrit dans Linear au lancement, c'est l'intégration GitHub qui gère le statut.
  - La session utilise le MCP Linear de Claude Code et Canopy n'injecte rien. Si ce MCP manque, la session affiche « Claude n'a pas accès à Linear dans cette session. ».
  - « Créer la PR » ajoute l'identifiant au titre.

Spec : `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-linear-connector-design.md`. Plan : `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-08-linear-connector.md`. Réponses de référence du vrai serveur (format, comportement de `patch`, normalisation du Markdown) : `tests/fixtures/linear/README.md`.

## Tests

- Unitaires : 1210/1210. Typecheck OK. Sur une machine chargée, `workspace`, `lsp` et `watch` dépassent parfois leur délai ; relancés seuls, ils passent.
- Bout en bout : 114/114. Le nouveau `linear.spec.ts` (8 scénarios) tourne sur un faux Linear qui rejoue les captures, actif seulement hors build packagé. Il couvre :
  - les identifiants identiques en local et dans Linear ;
  - les filtres ;
  - l'envoi en `patch` ;
  - l'échec, le redémarrage, puis le renvoi via ⟳ ;
  - le conflit avec un collègue ;
  - le lancement ;
  - la déconnexion avec des modifications en attente ;
  - le brouillon de commentaire.
- **Pas encore fait** : la vérification manuelle sur l'espace Linear perso (connexion réelle, modification simultanée Canopy et Linear, lancement puis PR reliée par l'intégration GitHub).

## Choix à relire

- Branche `feat/<id>-<titre>` (ma convention plus l'identifiant), plutôt que le `gitBranchName` de Linear qui contient le prénom.
- Titre et description partent à la sortie du champ ou à la fermeture de l'éditeur, jamais pendant la frappe.
- Les tickets lancés restent listés quel que soit le repo ouvert. Un ticket lancé puis annulé reste dans Terminé avec son vrai statut.
- Limites propres à Linear (titre 1000, 100 étiquettes de 200 caractères) : ce sont des estimations, et le serveur reste l'arbitre.

## Suites connues (non bloquantes)

- Un ticket supprimé dans Linear avec une modification en attente reste affiché sans possibilité d'abandonner la modification depuis l'éditeur.
- Quand seule la réécriture du Markdown par Linear efface une modification, l'éditeur annonce à tort « non appliquée » (sans perte).
- Les brouillons de commentaire sont perdus lors d'un redémarrage de mise à jour.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

nodes.body: `persist()` swallows every filesystem error and `save()` continues into `schedule()`, so an edit can be sent to Linear even when `linear-pending.json` was not written. A disk-full or permission failure followed by a crash can therefore lose a remotely applied edit, violating the write-before-send guarantee and the queue's restart safety. Persistence failure needs to prevent the send (and surface a pending/error result) rather than merely logging it.

Corrigé dans bca8602 : quand l'écriture de `linear-pending.json` échoue juste avant un envoi, rien n'est envoyé. La modification reste en mémoire et `save()` répond `pending` avec « Impossible d’enregistrer la modification sur le disque : … ». Le prochain `save`/`retryAll`/`retryFailed` réécrit la file avant d'envoyer. Tous les chemins d'envoi passent par ce contrôle.

This only reports typed Linear text to the main process; it does not make that text durable. The update collector flushes the local-ticket savers, but it does not flush `LinearSaver.commit()`, and the quit/update paths have no other handoff for an open Linear editor. Consequently, confirming quit or restarting for an update while the title/description is focused discards the typed text even though it was counted as unsaved. Add the Linear savers to the same flush/handoff path (or persist their drafts) before allowing the process to stop.

Corrigé dans 2e7c0f8 : avant le redémarrage d'une mise à jour, `flushLinearSavers()` remet le titre et la description tapés (éditeurs ouverts et textes restés bloqués) à la file sur disque, à côté de `flushSavers()`. Les brouillons de commentaire ne peuvent pas être envoyés automatiquement : ils sont désormais comptés à part, et la fenêtre de mise à jour annonce qu'ils seront perdus. La fermeture de l'app reste inchangée : elle annonce déjà « Seront perdus » pour un éditeur non enregistré.

### 🟡 Changes recommended Two critical data-loss paths remain: persistence failures can still allow sends, and focused Linear edits are not flushed or handed off before quit or restart.
2 open issues - [Prevent sending edits when queue persistence fails](https://github.com/BastienPailloux/canopy/pull/9#discussion_r4507791550) · New - [Flush Linear editor drafts before quit or update](https://github.com/BastienPailloux/canopy/pull/9#discussion_r4507791565) · New
What changed in this PR This pull request adds Linear integration to Canopy, including OAuth/MCP connectivity, synchronized assigned tickets, conflict-aware editing, persistent edit queuing, comments, and worktree launch flows. **Changes:** - Adds encrypted OAuth credentials, MCP communication, caching, synchronization, and queued Linear edits. - Integrates Linear issues into the Tickets UI with filtering, editing, comments, source-aware keys, and launch support. - Extends session prompts and notices, branch links, quit/update handling, and automated test and fixture coverage. commit.message:
docs: add Linear connector design (step 3)

Linear tickets assigned to me, mixed with local tickets, editable and
launchable from Canopy, through the official Linear MCP server.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): loopback-only callback with state, keep tokens on expiry

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

feat(linear): edit queue with description patches

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): never double-apply a resent edit, hold only the stuck field

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

feat(linear): list sync with cache and departures

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): sync can be cleared on disconnect

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): a refresh after clear starts fresh

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

feat(linear): launch a Linear ticket

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

feat(linear): IPC and app wiring

registerLinearIpc exposes the linear:* channels (validated in main) through
window.canopy, emits linear:changed on sync, queue and connection changes.
CANOPY_FAKE_LINEAR replays the fixtures like CANOPY_FAKE_QUERY. At start:
resume, resend the queue, refresh. Pending Linear edits make quitting ask.
Shared Linear types moved to src/shared/linear.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): app-wide launched set, safer disconnect and resume

The launched set kept listed by LinearSync is now app-wide (every linked
issue whose branch still exists, per root), so switching repo no longer
fakes a departure. Link read failures never hide the list. A forced
disconnect drops the queue only once the tokens are gone. A stale resume
never overwrites a newer connect. description.base is capped. A launched
issue reassigned while launched departs as reassigned once unlaunched.
Quit wording says the edits stay queued.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): own id from whoami, launched set ready before every refresh

Every refresh from the Linear IPC goes through one helper that recomputes the
launched set first; startLinear recomputes before looking at the resume
state. LinearSync takes Bastien's id from whoami (LinearConnection.userId)
instead of the first assignee of listMine, persisted with the cache.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

feat(linear): mixed ticket list with filters

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): guarded single refresh, per-repo links reset on switch

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

feat(linear): Linear ticket editor

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): editor keeps in-flight choices and ignores stale reads

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

feat(linear): launch panel, settings and session notice

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): MCP notice also on a reused session tab

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

test(linear): end-to-end

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): resend queued edits when Linear is reachable again

A refresh that reaches Linear resends the entries whose last send failed
(held fields stay held); system resume triggers a refresh.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): a start without network stays connected-intent and recovers on refresh

resume() reports 'offline' with the reason when tokens are stored but Linear
cannot be reached; every refresh tries the tokens again, then resends the
queue. Settings shows the reason and Déconnecter, never « Connecter Linear ».

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): launched issues and issues with unsent edits stay listed

One visibility rule (listGroup) in shared/linear.ts for main and renderer:
a kept issue with a hidden status (Canceled, Duplicate) shows in Terminé
with its Linear name. Issues with pending edits are kept like launched ones
(even deleted in Linear) until their queue is empty; then the departure
notice gives the true reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): a patch Linear ignores is held, and lost parameters are reported

The connection check also verifies save_issue.patch/id and
list_issues.assignee/cursor in the tool schemas. A patch save answered with
the description read just before (normalised) is held with both versions
(« Linear n’a pas appliqué la modification »), never reported sent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): edit queue re-plans before a lone resend, rewrites good entries, names uncertain conflicts

- After a refused combined save, the description is re-read and re-planned
  before going alone: a partly applied save never applies insert ops twice.
- A queue file with malformed entries is rewritten with the good ones at load.
- The uncertain-resend conflict has its own reason (UNCERTAIN_REASON), shown
  by the editor through conflictHint().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): comment drafts and every stranded editor text are kept and counted

- A comment being typed is kept per issue (back in the next editor) and
  counts as unsaved until posted; text typed during the send stays.
- Closed editors' savers with unsent text are kept as a list per issue:
  none overwrites another, so every one counted at quit can be reopened.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): label edits keep a colleague's labels; Linear's own limits

- LinearChange.labels is { base, next }: main re-reads the issue and applies
  Bastien's additions and removals to Linear's current set (applyLabels);
  queued label edits chain from the first base; nothing is sent when Linear
  already has the set.
- IPC validation uses LINEAR_MAX_TITLE/LABELS/LABEL (1000/100/200) from
  shared/linear.ts instead of the local-ticket limits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

refactor(linear): one description normalisation shared by main and the editor

normalizeDescription/sameDescription move to shared/linear.ts; the
renderer's own sameText (which also stripped no-break spaces Linear keeps)
is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): quit says which Linear edits wait for a decision

Held entries (conflict, refusal) add « Certaines modifications Linear
attendent ta décision dans l’éditeur. »; the « partiront dès que Linear sera
joignable » sentence is kept for the entries with a field that will go.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): settings offer Déconnecter while expired or offline; new missing-tools text

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): refresh when an issue leaves the edit queue, so a kept issue departs with its notice

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

Merge origin/develop into feat/linear-tickets

Brings #6 (CLAUDE.md), #7 (claude.ai mockups linked to tickets) and #8
(sessions start in the last picked mode).

Resolutions:
- main/index.ts: both imports; registerIpc gets the shared TicketStore
  and the new MockupStore; the Linear wiring is unchanged.
- preload/index.ts, shared/api.ts: the Linear and the mockup surfaces side by side.
- App.tsx: connectLinear and connectMockups both run; the Tickets view
  keeps OpenTicket (TicketKey), the Mockups view is added.
- store.ts: selectedTicket/openTicket stay TicketKey; the mockup fields
  are added (pendingMockupTicket is a local ticket ID).
- LaunchPanel.tsx: « Joindre les maquettes liées » for local tickets only:
  a mockup links a local ticket by its bare ID, which a Linear issue can
  share (CAN-7), so a Linear issue gets no mockups. No « Passer En cours »
  for Linear, as before.
- launchFlow.ts: runLaunch sends launchText (prompt + mockups), runLinearLaunch
  unchanged (linearLaunchPrompt, expectLinear); shared showLaunched.
- tickets.css: the branch's Linear block, then develop's mockup block.
- launchFlow.test.ts: both suites.
- TicketKey migration of #7's code: MockupsScreen opens local:<id>,
  launchFromMockup selects local:<id> (mockupStore.test updated).

#8's remembered mode (tab.mode) and this branch's expectLinear are separate
start options of startSession: they compose.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

perf(linear): list without descriptions, 250 per page

Bastien's list and an issue's sub-issues ask for the list fields only
(no description) at Linear's maximum page size. The description is read
with get_issue (editor, launch prompt, edit rebase), never from the list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

perf(linear): look up departed issues five at a time, a deleted launched issue only once

Issues missing from the assigned list are looked up in batches of 5
instead of one after the other. A launched issue Linear says no longer
exists departs once (« introuvable ») and its link is dropped, so later
refreshes never ask for it again. One with an unsent edit stays until
Bastien decides, as before; a failed lookup forgets nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

perf(linear): an open editor reads the issue again only when Linear changed it

linear:changed now names the issues touched ({ ids }: a sync commit's
changed, added, removed or departed issues, the issue whose edit queue
changed, the departures acknowledged); a connection change sends {}.

The open editor reads its queue (local) when its issue is named, and the
issue itself (get_issue, sub-issue and comment pages) only for an event
naming no issue or when the list holds a newer copy than the one shown:
its own save answer is reused, never read back. Reads are debounced
(300 ms). The list re-reads without listing every linked repo's branches
for an event that names no linked issue; a launch reads the links itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

perf(linear): skip the focus refresh within 30 s of the last sync

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <user@example.com>

fix(linear): keep a launched ticket's branch link when Linear cannot find it

« Not found » also comes from a lost team access or another workspace, so
dropping the link was irreversible for an issue that still exists. The
sync now keeps the launched issues not found aside (in its cache): each
departs once as « introuvable », is not asked for again, and keeps its
link and branch. The set is emptied on a connect, an account change and a
disconnect; an issue back in the list is listed again.
